_purpose: The strict envelope contract for states produced after Phase 40. RESEARCH Q6 section 3 plus D-16. Changing this file is an envelope change and needs a recorded decision. v2.10 Wave 1 (41-06) added the optional `members` finding key (D-14) — a recorded decision, see SUPERSESSIONS-v2.10.md entry 007. Rollback: a scorer without this key drops `members` at `_shape_finding` and carries the representative unchanged; absorbed-member evidence is lost on rollback (accepted downgrade, test_score.py TestRollbackStateCompat). v2.11 Phase 46 (CARRY-01/02/03, CONTEXT D-01/D-02/D-04/D-06/D-08) added finding `snapshot` and `kept_open`, pass `resolved`, root `decisions` and root `fix_verdicts`; `medium_acknowledgments` stays root_required and is legacy read-only after Phase 46. v2.12 Phase 53 (QUIET-06/07, CONTEXT D-04/D-13, R8/R10) added the optional finding key `needs_verification` (the Needs-verification item: trigger/path/consequence/symbol), the band literal `needs-verification` with orchestrator_score 0, and the rollback marker: every Needs-verification row's `members` holds exactly its own lane ref with the STRING `obligation` `needs-verification`. A reader without Needs-verification support refuses that state (`refused: malformed state: obligation`) instead of counting the undecided item as nothing — an undecided Needs-verification item blocks APPROVED across a plugin rollback (R10); see `_rollback.phase53_nv_downgrade` for the procedure, which refuses to downgrade while any Needs-verification item is undecided (test_score.py TestRollbackNeedsVerification pins the shipped 2.11.1 reader). Phase-53-format state lives at `.turingmind/state/format-53/<the shipped key>` (`statepath.resolve_current`), a path no shipped 2.11.x resolver can produce. v2.13 Phase 56 (VFIX-03/04/06, CONTEXT D-07/D-09) added the optional finding key `recheck_settled` — the scorer's record that a reviewer answered still-applies on an independent or bound re-check, with the blob fingerprint of the code it judged, so the item is not re-asked until that code changes. Rollback: a reader without the key refuses the state (`finding_closed`), the same fail-closed direction as Phase 53; remove the key from every finding per `_rollback.phase56_added`.
_scope: This schema proves the ENVELOPE shape is stable. It does NOT prove orchestration or rendered reports are unchanged: those are the scorer leg (test_score.py goldens), the script leg (per-script goldens), and the trace leg (plan 40-13). One of four legs.

_rollback.procedure: To run a plugin older than Phase 46 against a Phase-46-produced state, first copy the state file to `<state>.pre-downgrade.bak`, then remove exactly the keys listed in `phase46_added`: the root keys from the root object, the pass keys from every `passes[]` entry, and the finding keys from every finding in every pass. Nothing else changes: every scored field and every pass is preserved, and the `.pre-downgrade.bak` copy keeps the Phase-46 evidence (decisions, resolutions, snapshots), so re-upgrading is a copy back. The older plugin's Finalize reads only `medium_acknowledgments`, so it will re-ask about findings whose owner decision lived in `decisions`; that is the only behavioral loss and it is non-destructive. For a Phase-53-produced state, run `phase53_nv_downgrade` FIRST (it removes the `phase53_added` key from the Needs-verification rows it converts), then this procedure. For a Phase-56-produced state, also remove the finding keys listed in `phase56_added` from every finding in every pass (a dropped still-applies memory only means the item may be re-asked).
_rollback.phase53_nv_downgrade: To run a plugin older than Phase 53 against a Phase-53-produced state: Step 0 (refusal) — run the CURRENT plugin's `carry_state.py finalize-counts` on the state file; if `undecided_nv` is non-zero, STOP with a non-zero exit and a plain message listing `undecided_nv_hashes`; write nothing and take no backup — the owner decides those items (confirm, dismiss or defer, by number) on a `--finalize` with the current plugin first, because an older collector reads the canonical at `file:line` only and an older scorer moves a nullable-line or relocated item into fixed-since-last, which would make an undecided item disappear and let APPROVED be written. Only a state with `undecided_nv == 0` proceeds. Step 1 — copy the Phase-53 state file (the `format-53/` location, `statepath.resolve_current`) to `<state>.pre-downgrade.bak`; the Phase-53 file itself is NEVER modified or deleted by this procedure — it is the recoverable original. Step 2 — on a COPY: for every finding in every `passes[]` entry whose `band` is `needs-verification`: remove the `needs_verification` key and the `members` key; if the finding is in the LAST pass and its `status` is one of {new, persisted, needs-recheck}, set its `band` to `warning`, and when it carries a `snapshot` set the snapshot's `band` to `warning` too (the snapshot mirrors the row's band, exactly as the scorer would write it; this is what makes the older reader see the owner decision's `needs-verification` evidence band as changed) — the older reader has no uncertainty band; a warning is counted by number and is never cleared by a bulk Dismiss all / Defer all. Nothing else changes: every other field, every pass, `decisions` and `fix_verdicts` are preserved verbatim. Step 3 — write the converted copy to the OLD location (the shipped resolver's key for the same scope: `statepath.resolve`, i.e. the flat `<repo>-<branch-slug>.json` / `<PHASE_ID>.json` or `by-mode/all/<12hex>.json` file directly under `.turingmind/state/`); Normally no file exists there: the current plugin's forward migration moved the pre-upgrade file aside, no-clobber, as `<old>.migrated-format-53` (or `-2`, `-3`, …) once its copy into `format-53/` was verified, so an older plugin cannot resume it. If a file does exist there, copy it to `<old>.pre-downgrade.bak` FIRST — never overwrite without a backup. Alternative to Steps 1-3, only for a review the current plugin has NOT closed (no `<format-53 state>.archived-*` file): to return to exactly the pre-upgrade state, copy the newest `<old>.migrated-format-53[-N]` archive back to `<old>` (it is the recoverable original; keep the archive). Every decision and pass recorded under the current plugin is then absent from the older plugin's view, and Step 0 still applies first. Every converted row is a DECIDED item (Step 0 guarantees it); its owner decision carries evidence band `needs-verification`, so the older plugin treats it as stale and asks again — the safe direction — and if an older ordinary review moves the converted row into fixed-since-last, its decision remains in `decisions`. The older plugin never reads the `format-53/` location (its resolver cannot produce that path), so the Phase-53 state is untouched throughout. Re-upgrading needs no copy: the new plugin's Phase 0.5 prefers the `format-53/` file when present (the forward migration copies old -> new ONLY when the new location is absent, and never copies over an existing `format-53/` file); an old-location file the downgraded plugin wrote is moved aside, no-clobber, as `<old>.migrated-format-53[-N]`. Decisions taken during the downgrade live in that archive and may be merged into the Phase-53 file's `decisions` by hand — they will be asked again under the new reader for the same evidence reason.
